note: Pins BITARRAY.md's operation set at widths 32/64/128/256, plus the mixed-width, invalid-width and no-polynomial cases.  Error cases pin an expected ERROR CODE, not a value: BITARRAY.md 5 makes the code set closed and identical in every port, so a port that fails for the right reason is distinguishable from one that fails for the wrong one.  Operands are structured rather than pseudo-random -- a rotation or a truncation that loses an octet is invisible against a uniform operand.  NO PORT IMPLEMENTS THIS YET: see BITARRAY.md 7 and 8 for how ports join the gating set.
truncation_rule: HIGH bits -- the big-endian PREFIX (BITARRAY.md 4.4).  This settles the TODO #313 split: Python and C's declared narrow constants already say high bits; Go's RnlKdfDC[32-n/8:] is the outlier.
